t: Brightest Position on Street: Sweep Line over Lamp Endpoints
o:
**Understanding the problem**

Lamp i lights every integer point of [position_i - range_i, position_i + range_i]; return the smallest position lit by the most lamps. Example 1 produces intervals [-5,-1], [-1,3], [0,6]; brightness 2 holds at -1 and again on [0,3], so the smaller coordinate -1 wins. Example 2 stacks a point lamp [1,1] on top of [-1,1], making position 1 the unique maximum. Example 3 shows a lone lamp lighting its whole span equally, so its left endpoint -1 is returned. Coordinates reach 10^8 with up to 10^5 lamps, so visiting every street position is impossible; fortunately brightness only changes at interval boundaries, and the maximum always begins at some lamp's start point.
k: Brightness changes only at lamp starts (position - range) and just past ends (position + range + 1); the brightest position can always be taken to be some start coordinate.
Compress each lamp into two events — +1 at its start and -1 just past its end — sort them, and sweep with a running counter like a sparse difference array.
Finish processing all events at a coordinate before recording it, and update only on strict improvement so the smallest position wins ties automatically.

a.i: Since brightness only jumps upward at start coordinates, some lamp start is a brightest point; evaluating the number of covering lamps at every interval boundary therefore suffices, keeping the smallest maximizer. Sorting candidates and counting coverage naively costs quadratic time — perfectly clear, but with 10^5 lamps it means billions of operations.
s: Gather candidate coordinates: for each lamp, position - range and position + range + 1.
For each candidate x, count lamps satisfying position - range <= x <= position + range.
Track the best count seen; because candidates ascend, strict improvement locks in the smallest brightest coordinate.
a.t: O(n^2) — up to 2n candidates each checked against n lamps; too slow at n = 10^5.

a.i: Convert each lamp into two delta events and sort them once. Sweeping left to right while accumulating deltas reproduces the brightness of every segment between consecutive event coordinates in O(1) amortized per event. Recording a candidate only after exhausting all events of a coordinate, and only on strict improvement, yields exactly the smallest brightest position without extra tie-break logic.
s: Create events (start, +1) and (end + 1, -1) for every lamp.
Sort events by coordinate, breaking ties by putting +1 ahead of -1.
Sweep: absorb all events sharing one coordinate into the running brightness.
After each coordinate group, if the brightness exceeds the best seen, record the coordinate.
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting the 2n events dominates; the sweep itself is linear.

w:
**Takeaway**

Go straight to the event sweep in an interview: it is short, O(n log n), and generalizes naturally (weighted lamps, streaming insertions via an ordered map). Pitfalls: the closing decrement belongs at end + 1 because ranges are inclusive; all events sharing one coordinate must be consumed before comparing; and strict-greater updates preserve the smallest position for free. Under the stated bounds position + range + 1 stays inside 32-bit range, but double-check in fixed-width languages. Follow-ups: brightest position after lamp failures, or incremental lamp additions.
